name: Kang-Li Viper E-Bike
description: The most common motorized personal vehicle in Tier 1-2 districts. A stripped-down electric bicycle with a 2kW hub motor, bare aluminum frame, and a battery that lasts about 40 km if you're gentle. Most Vipers on the street have been repaired so many times that no original parts remain. They're ugly, they're slow, and they're freedom — the difference between a thirty-minute commute and a two-hour walk.
propulsion: Electric hub motor, removable lithium-polymer battery
speed: 35 km/h top speed, 20 km/h realistic with rider weight
cost: Φ200 new (nobody buys new), Φ40-80 used, Φ15 from a chop shop
armament: None. The lock is the most valuable component.
common_usage: Delivery riders, gig workers, students, anyone who needs to move faster than walking but can't afford a car.
story_hooks: A delivery rider's Viper has been stolen and rebuilt so many times it has parts from every district — it's a map of the city in component form
Someone is sabotaging Viper batteries in a specific district, stranding gig workers and killing their income
physical_description: A skeletal aluminum frame painted in faded industrial gray, its welds visible and rough. The 2kW hub motor whines in the rear wheel, surrounded by mismatched spoke repairs and a chain held together with wire and prayer. A cracked polymer seat sits atop the frame, and the battery pack—a bulky rectangle of scuffed lithium cells—is bolted directly to the downtube with no aesthetic pretense.
